newsitem.title: USA: Sri Lanka may switch to Canada/Australia wheat.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka may switch to Canada/Australia wheat.

text.p: Sri Lanka may be seeking Canadian and Australian wheat after relying on U.S. wheat to meet its recent needs, several U.S. exporters said.

U.S. exporters reported September 4 that Sri Lanka had bought 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for the current 1996-97 marketing year, split between 50,000 tonnes of hard red winter and 50,000 tonnes of soft red winter wheats, prime U.S. grades.
Exporters said the main options on origin had been United States, Canada or Australian wheat for Sept/Oct shipments.
"Initially it might have been U.S., and now they are going to Canada with it," a senior export trader said.
But the Sri Lanka sale was initially full option, "so it could go anywhere," he said.
Lower prices were prompting the switch, exporters said.

"It's the same song, different verse," a second U.S. exporter said, referring to lackluster U.S. wheat exports now that European supplies are available and Australian and Argentine supplies will be on the market by December.
The second exporter said he suspected Sri Lanka would now take 50,000 tonnes of soft white wheat from Australia and 50,000 tonnes of hard red spring wheat from Canada.
"The transaction was fairly new, as far as the switch goes. I think the switch is being completed now," the exporter said.
"I heard the same thing," a third trader at a U.S. export firm said. "But I don't know at all what constitutes fact or rumor in regards to this."
On the original tender, Sri Lanka requested delivery in September for the soft white wheat and October for the hard red spring wheat.
Canadian spring wheat on the St. Lawrence was being quoted at about $170 a tonne FOB on Wednesday, compared to U.S. hard red wheat at the Gulf at $173 FOB and U.S. spring wheat at $178 FOB.
